title: Empyrean / Aether Bus Protocol (Phase 1 thin slice — SEED)
description: Source-of-truth message schema for the Aether bus (the Empyrean suite's shared protocol). SEED: the envelope, handshake, events, the symbol primitive, and a representative set of ops are schematized here; the remaining per-method param/result schemas (see contract/protocol.md §6) are completed mechanically during emulator conformance. The authoritative live method set is whatever `initialize` advertises. PRECEDENCE (protocol.md D14): this file is NORMATIVE for wire shapes — which keys exist, their JSON types and ranges, whether they are required — while protocol.md is normative for semantics and behaviour. A disagreement between the two is a spec bug to be fixed by amendment in the pass that finds it; until amended, this file governs what goes on the wire. It is not a place to introduce behaviour: a shape here with no counterpart in protocol.md is an un-specced field, and §8's ban on unilateral invention applies. The two are amended together.

hex.description: Address or byte blob as a hex string (D9 category 1).

symbolName.description: A symbol's IDENTIFYING spelling, exactly as the listing writes it (protocol.md §4). It MUST round-trip: passing it back as lookup_symbol's `name`, or as any method's `symbol` param, MUST resolve to the same symbol — which is D7 made operable. The pattern forbids exactly one thing: a trailing `+$<hex>` displacement suffix. A displacement belongs in the reply's OWN numeric field (`disp`, `symbolDisp`), and a name carrying it duplicates a number the same reply already holds, inside a string a client would have to parse to get it back — §2.4's 'MUST NOT parse' and the same defect §11.5 struck run_to.stoppedAtFrame for. Mangling is NOT forbidden: `$engine.boot$EntryPoint$wait_dma` is a legitimate identifying name and the pattern accepts it, because `$` is only rejected in the `+$hex`-at-the-end position. Expressed as a pattern rather than as a sentence for D14's stated reason — a schema either accepts a message or does not.

hash64.description: A 64-bit FNV-1a fingerprint, spelled as a hex string of exactly 16 digits (protocol.md §6's '16-hex FNV-1a each', read through D9 category 1 — a hex value on this bus is a hex string). A fingerprint is compared, never computed on, so the fixed width is part of the type: a 15-digit answer is a leading zero somebody dropped, and two servers that disagree about padding produce fingerprints that never match.

handle.description: An opaque handle (D9 category 4): a value the server issues purely so the client can hand it back — a checkpoint `id`, a list `cursor`. A string, deliberately: a client MUST NOT parse, order, compare or do arithmetic on one, and a number would invite exactly that. The representation is the server's business (protocol.md §6.1).

items.description: This page of the list. Item shape is the owning method's business; the envelope around it is not.

total.description: How many items exist, not how many were returned.

returned.description: items.length, restated so a client can compare it to `total` without counting.

truncated.description: REQUIRED EVEN WHEN FALSE (protocol.md §2.4 clause (a)): absence and `false` must not both mean 'you have everything', for the same reason droppedEvents is always present (§2.3).

cursor.description: Continuation handle. Present ONLY on methods that accept a cursor param — §2.4 clause (b): a method that accepts no continuation MUST NOT emit one, because a token that can never be handed back trains clients that handles are ignorable and publishes the server's position for nothing (D9 category 4's opacity argument). Behaviour is normative (§2.4 clause (c)); representation is the server's.

limit.description: The page ceiling the server actually applied, which is not necessarily the one the client asked for.

boundedList.description: The container for a list that is a FIELD of a result (protocol.md §2.4). A list that IS the whole result keeps the flat spelling its §6 row gives it — the array under its own name with total/returned/limit/truncated/cursor? as siblings — which is emulator/checkpoint_list. Identical field set, identical rules; only the nesting differs. Governs POLICY-bounded lists (a bound the server chose). A STRUCTURALLY bounded list — emulator/pixel_attribution's `candidates`, capped at 4 by the video hardware — takes neither the flag nor the cursor, because a list that cannot be partial has no partial-list failure mode (§2.4 clause (d)).

running.description: Whether the machine was free-running when this payload was built.

stamp.description: The machine stamp (protocol.md §2.2, D11). Present on every result, every error.data, and every event's params. Emulated clocks only — never wall-clock. Applied envelope-level after the handler returns, overwriting any same-named key. What a `frame` IS — the basis these clocks are expressed in — is advertised once in the initialize result as `timingBasis` (D16).

droppedEvents.description: Server→client events discarded on THIS connection since it opened (protocol.md §2.3, D17). Monotonically non-decreasing, cumulative, and always present — 0 is the answer, not the absence of one. Not part of the stamp (the stamp is a machine coordinate every connection sees identically; this is a per-connection fact) and never present on an event.

replyFields.description: The full envelope field set carried by every SUCCESS result and every error.data: the machine stamp (§2.2) plus the dropped-event counter (§2.3). Events carry `stamp` only.

method.$comment: Role-namespaced, snake_case, digits allowed after the first character (D3). The digits matter: the previous pattern `^([a-z]+/)?[a-z_]+$` rejected three catalogued methods — emulator/z80_read, emulator/z80_write, emulator/z80_registers — and nothing caught it because nothing validated against this file. Fixed 2026-08-15 (protocol.md §11.2); checked against every method name in protocol.md §6. Request methods only: EVENT names are camelCase (emulator/romReloaded, §3) and are matched by #/$defs/notification, which deliberately carries no pattern.

id.$comment: NULL IS PERMITTED HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE (CR-15, protocol.md §11.4). JSON-RPC 2.0 §5: 'If there was an error in detecting the id in the Request Object (e.g. Parse error/Invalid Request), it MUST be Null.' protocol.md §2 adopts JSON-RPC 2.0 wholesale and §8 item 2 makes it a conformance item, so the adopted standard MANDATED a value this schema excluded — a server answering a -32700 or a -32600 had no conformant option at all. Deliberately NOT widened in #/$defs/id: a request must carry a real id (an id-less request is a notification, matched by #/$defs/notification), and a success response echoes the request's id, so null is meaningless in both. The `allOf` below narrows it further, to the two codes that mandate it.

allOf.$comment: A null id is permitted ONLY on the two codes decided before a request object exists: -32700 (parse error) and -32600 (invalid request). Every other code answers a request the server DID parse, so a real id was available to echo and a null one is a correlation bug — the client cannot match the failure to the call that caused it, which is the silent-wrong-answer class this contract exists to prevent (D11's argument, applied to the error path). Expressed as if/then rather than in prose alone so it is mechanically enforced, per D14's reason for making the schema the tiebreaker at all.

code.description: -32700 parse | -32600 invalid request | -32601 method not found | -32602 invalid params | -32603 internal | -32000 not wired | -32004 addr out of range | -32005 invalid state for this operation | -32010 timeout | -32012 no symbols | -32013 symbol not found | -32015 unsupported protocol version

reason.description: Machine-readable discriminant. REQUIRED for -32005, e.g. machineRunning | checkpointCapReached | unknownCheckpoint (protocol.md §5).

data.description: Always present: it carries the machine stamp (D11) and droppedEvents (D17), plus any structured context.

cap.description: Max live checkpoints; the server refuses at this count with -32005 (D13 rule 3).

checkpoints.description: protocol.md §6.1. An object, not a bare flag, because the cap must be discoverable before a client plans around it.

methods.description: Authoritative live method set — replaces the removed list_ops (D4). This array IS the count of the server's surface; no number in prose tracks it.

standard.description: Video standard, lowercase. Defined values today: 'ntsc', 'pal'. Deliberately not an enum — a client SHOULD branch on the numbers below, and the label exists so a human reading a log knows what they are looking at.

mclkPerFrame.description: Master-clock ticks in one frame — the divisor that turns an mclk stamp into a frame index (896040 NTSC).

linesPerFrame.description: Scanlines in one frame, including blanking (262 NTSC).

timingBasis.description: REQUIRED (protocol.md §2.1, D16). What the `frame` in every stamp MEANS. A top-level key rather than a capability flag: it is not something a server may or may not support, it is what that server's stamps are expressed in. The numbers are normative, not just the label ('ntsc' alone does not say 262 lines or 263), and a server MUST derive them from the same constants its own frame arithmetic uses.

events.$comment: Event names are camelCase (romReloaded, never rom_reloaded) — protocol.md §3 and §10 decision 4. Every event's params also carries the machine stamp.

frames.description: Frames actually advanced. REQUIRED when reason is runFrames (protocol.md §3).

deadlineReached.description: True when the run ended on its bound rather than its condition (D12). Always true for runFrames.

buildId.description: reserved for the future build manifest

methods.$comment: THE TWELVE FRAGMENTS ADDED 2026-08-15 (protocol.md §11.5) — emulator/status, load_symbols, pause, resume, press, hold, release_all, read_vram, reload_rom, run_frames, screenshot, state_hash — were each written FROM THE AMENDED §6 ROW, never from a server's replies. That direction is the whole point: §8 forbids the emulator side to invent, and a fragment transcribed from what a server emits would encode the implementation as the contract, which is the inversion this document exists to prevent (§0: 'the contract leads; the emulator implements against it'). Where a shipped key had no §6 row it was ruled first — registered, pinned, or struck — and only then schematized.

emulator/status.$comment: protocol.md §6 (status / misc). `running` is NOT declared here: it is the machine stamp's (§2.2, D11), applied envelope-level after the handler returns and arriving through replyFields. §6's row lists it because the row predates D11; §2.2 is explicit that clients MUST NOT treat the stamp as a per-method field. Declaring it twice would invite a handler to think it owns the value.

frameToken.description: A JSON number under D9 category 2, and checked to be one: it is the emulated frame index, not a UI counter (protocol.md §11.2's 'what this pass deliberately did not change'). NOT a handle.

symbolAtPc.$comment: The BARE label at the PC — protocol.md §4's naming rule, which binds every symbol field on this bus. The displacement is `symbolDisp` and appears nowhere else; a rendering like 'Obj_Spring+$4' is the two fields concatenated, and a client that wants it can build it.

symbolDisp.description: Registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5). Bytes past `symbolAtPc`; 0 is an exact hit. Present when symbolAtPc is.

romBytes.description: Size of the loaded cartridge image. Registered 2026-08-15.

romPath.description: Path to the loaded ROM on the SERVER's filesystem — a host-filesystem fact, which D8's trusted-local-developer trust model makes unremarkable (see §6's paths note). Null when no ROM has been loaded from a path.

symbolsPath.description: Path to the loaded listing, same treatment. Null when no listing is loaded.

emulator/load_symbols.$comment: protocol.md §4 and §6 (symbols). `binding` is §4's forward note, no longer forward.

moduleCount.description: How many modules the listing spans, beside the symbol count. Registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5).

binding.description: Whether the listing could be checked against the ROM image actually loaded. `match` = it passed the check; `indeterminate` = it could not be checked at all and was accepted UNVERIFIED. There is deliberately no `mismatch` value: a listing that positively binds to a DIFFERENT image is refused with -32602 and carries its binding in error.data, because D7's hazard is that a mismatched listing is not degraded information but confidently wrong information.

emulator/pause.$comment: protocol.md §6 (run-control). `wasRunning` registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5): it is D12's `reached` logic transposed — a result that reports nothing cannot distinguish 'I stopped it' from 'it was already stopped', and it is what lets a client make pause idempotent without a second round-trip.

wasRunning.description: Whether the machine was free-running BEFORE this call. Reports the transition, not the destination — the destination is known from the method name.

emulator/resume.$comment: protocol.md §6 (run-control). Mirror of emulator/pause; same field, same registration.

wasRunning.description: Whether the machine was free-running BEFORE this call.

emulator/press.$comment: protocol.md §6 (input). Named in §6's run-control state rule: it mutates the timeline (it holds buttons across a bounded run of frames), so it requires a paused machine and MUST fail -32005 machineRunning otherwise.

frames.description: Catalog ceiling. A given server's ACTUAL ceiling is initialize's limits.maxRunFrames, which it refuses above rather than clamping to (§2.1).

port.description: Which controller. Registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5) — the two-controller surface the catalog never grew. D9 category 2 (an index a client counts with). Defaults to 0 so every call written before this row existed keeps meaning what it meant.
Echoed on the result as well as accepted on the params: a reply that does not say which pad it acted on is unreadable in a two-client session, where the caller is not the only source of input.

emulator/hold.$comment: protocol.md §6 (input). NOT in the run-control state rule: hold sets pad state and advances nothing.

held.description: The buttons held on this port AFTER the call — the resulting set, not an echo of `buttons`. Registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5): hold has set-not-add semantics, and this is what makes that verifiable without a second round-trip. Deliberately NOT a boundedList: it is bounded at 8 by the controller, which is a structural bound (§2.4 clause (d)).

emulator/release_all.$comment: protocol.md §6 (input). NO RESULT KEYS, and that is a ruling rather than an omission: the reference server emitted `released: true`, a hardcoded constant that can never be false and carries zero bits, and it was REMOVED (§11.5) rather than registered. Removing it is not amputation — there was nothing attached. §6's row said `—` and still does, so this fragment is the row.

emulator/read_vram.$comment: protocol.md §6 (VRAM / CRAM / layers). The row is unchanged by this pass: its only surplus was a `caveat`, which §2.4 now defines once for the whole bus and which §2.4 clause 4 says a row need not enumerate. The fragment declares it anyway, because §8 item 20 closes results at test time and an undeclared caveat would fail that check.

emulator/reload_rom.$comment: protocol.md §6 (run-control). Named in §6's run-control state rule — it swaps the cartridge out from under whatever is executing — so it requires a paused machine. Emits emulator/romReloaded.

path.description: Omit to reload the image already loaded.

reloaded.description: The reload completed synchronously. Exactly one of `reloaded`/`queued` is present.

queued.description: The reload was accepted and will complete asynchronously; the romReloaded event is the completion signal.

romBytes.description: Size of the image now in the machine. Registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5), same key and same meaning as status.romBytes — it is the confirmation that the file read is the cartridge loaded.

symbolsDropped.description: The loaded symbol listing stopped binding to the new image and was dropped. Registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5), and it is the strongest registration in that pass: D7 is this contract's most emphatic decision, and a reload that silently invalidates the symbol table while a client keeps resolving names against it is precisely D7's named hazard. REQUIRED, present even when false — absence and false must not both mean 'your symbols are fine' (§2.3's argument).

emulator/run_frames.$comment: protocol.md §6 (run-control) and §3. Requires a paused machine (-32005 machineRunning otherwise). Emits emulator/resumed, then emulator/stopped with reason 'runFrames' — NOT the nearest-looking 'step' (§8 item 13). This method's reply carried no surplus at all on the 2026-08-15 sweep, which §11.5 notes is not luck.

frames.description: Catalog default 1. The server's ceiling is initialize's limits.maxRunFrames, refused above rather than clamped.

emulator/screenshot.$comment: protocol.md §6 (status / misc). Five keys registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5) against a row that said only `path`. Neither this method nor reload_rom was reached by the ruling that opened that pass; both are ruled there.

path.description: Where to write. Omit and the server chooses; the chosen path is always echoed.

format.description: The encoding written. A constant on any one server today and registered anyway — unlike the vacuous `released` struck from release_all, its value space is genuinely open, and §6's row already anticipates a second representation ('the HTTP binding MAY return image content inline'). A client that must infer the format from a file extension is guessing.

width.description: Not constant: H32 is 256 and H40 is 320, and a client indexing a pixel out of the file gets it wrong on one of them.

bytes.description: Size written, on the checkpoint.bytes precedent — how a caller knows the write completed rather than merely that a path was chosen.

source.description: WHICH PICTURE WAS SERVED. `raster` = the frame the scanline path actually drew. `stateRender` = re-derived from VDP state as it stands now, the honest fallback before any whole frame has been drawn. Provenance, and the register case rather than a nicety: §6's pixel_attribution prose already spends a paragraph on why the two legitimately differ and why pausing does NOT reconcile them (measured over 17 test ROMs). A stateRender picture silently labelled as the frame is the silent wrong answer D11 exists to prevent.

caveat.description: protocol.md §2.4 — and this method is the shape §2.4's advisory says to copy: it warns only when `source` is stateRender, rather than emitting a constant string on every reply.

emulator/state_hash.$comment: protocol.md §6 (status / misc). The five fingerprints cover VDP state only.

result.$comment: §6's row spells each hash '16-hex FNV-1a'. Read through D9 category 1 — a hex value on this bus is a hex string — that is $defs/hex narrowed to exactly 16 digits, which is the pattern used below rather than a bare 16-character form.

framebuffer.$comment: Present if and only if the includeFramebuffer param was true.

framebufferSource.description: Which picture was hashed — the same enum and the same meaning as emulator/screenshot's `source`, registered in the same pass (§11.5) and for a sharper version of the same reason: a fingerprint whose input provenance is unstated is worse than one that is simply wrong, because two machines can disagree on it for a reason that has nothing to do with either machine. Present if and only if `framebuffer` is.

result.$comment: protocol.md §4, rewritten 2026-08-15 (§11.5). The anyOf is §4's one structural invariant: a result MUST carry either `addr` or `otherMatches` — the call either resolved to a location or offers candidates, and a reply that does neither has answered nothing while reporting success. Nothing else is required across all three result shapes, so nothing else is listed as required here; the per-shape obligations are prose in §4, which D14 makes normative for semantics.

addr.$comment: The resolved bus address. Absent only on the prefix-fallback shape, where nothing was resolved and inventing one would be a silent wrong answer.

demangled.description: The readable spelling, for display to a human. Present when it differs from `name`. NOT guaranteed unique and NOT guaranteed to round-trip — `ambiguous` is how a server says so.

disp.description: Queried address minus the resolved symbol's address; 0 is an exact hit. Address direction only. This is the ONLY place the displacement appears — see `name`.

query.description: The `addr` or `name` the request asked for, echoed. Load-bearing rather than decorative: on the address direction the answer's `addr` is the SYMBOL's address, not the queried one, so without this the reply does not record what was asked; on the prefix shape it is the reply's only trace of the request. A string in both directions (a hex address is a string, D9 category 1).

exact.description: REQUIRED on the name direction and present in BOTH cases: true = a symbol has exactly this name, false = these are prefix guesses. Not omitted on the true branch — a field that appears only in the unusual case is a field nobody reads (D16's argument, and D17's).

ambiguous.description: Several DIFFERENT addresses share this symbol's demangled spelling, so the readable name does not identify a location. The machine-readable half of the corresponding caveat, and it exists because §2.4 forbids parsing the caveat.

synthetic.description: The resolved label is toolchain plumbing (an alignment pad, a synthetic block scope) rather than a name a person wrote. Address direction. A client showing a PC to a human needs to know the nearest label is a pad.

rawAddr.$comment: The listing's own unmasked spelling of `addr` where the two differ — a 68000 listing writes work RAM as 0xFFFF8CFA while the machine drives 24 address lines and puts 0x00FF8CFA on the bus. Carried so a client can round-trip a value back to the listing text. `addr` is the one to compute with.

caveat.description: protocol.md §2.4. Conditional here, correctly: it fires on a non-zero displacement, on an ambiguous readable name, and on the prefix fallback.

otherMatches.$comment: CR-14, adopted 2026-08-15. Was `{type: array, items: {type: string}}`, which the reference server had never emitted: a bare array is exactly what §2.4 clause (a) forbids on a method §4 itself says truncates at 5, and bare strings would drop the `addr` the client asked for. The bound is a POLICY bound (this spec chose 5; a symbol table holds thousands) so total/truncated are mandatory — and there is NO cursor and NO nextCursor, because lookup_symbol accepts no continuation param and §2.4 clause (b) forbids a token that can never be handed back. Symbol BROWSING, if ever wanted, is a new cursored method and its own change request; lookup_symbol is a resolution primitive.

name.$comment: Same contract as the top-level `name` — this is the value a client hands back to resolve the match, so it is the round-trippable spelling and not the readable one.

items.description: ONE pinned item shape. The reference server emitted two — {name,addr} on the exact-demangled branch and {name,demangled,addr} on the prefix branch — which is a client having to discover which branch it is on in order to read the list.

emulator/registers.$comment: protocol.md §6 (memory & Z80). PROPERTIES ADDED 2026-08-15 (§11.5): this fragment previously declared NONE, and stood in for them with `additionalProperties: {$ref hex}` plus a hand-listing of the four envelope fields to stop that catch-all rejecting them. The catch-all is gone with the properties: it was open in the direction that mattered (any misspelled register name passed, so long as its value looked like hex) and closed in the direction D5 protects (a future registered non-hex key would have been rejected). Enumerating the file is what makes `usp`/`ssp` — registered in the same pass — checkable at all.

result.description: The 68000 architectural register file: d0–d7, a0–a7, pc, sp, usp, ssp, sr — every one a hex string (D9 category 1). The envelope fields (§2.2 stamp, §2.3 droppedEvents) arrive through replyFields and are numbers/booleans; they are NOT listed here, because nothing in this fragment rejects them any more.

a7.$comment: A7 is the ACTIVE stack pointer — the same value as `sp` — because the 68000 selects between usp and ssp by the S bit. Both spellings are carried because both are how people read a register dump; `usp` and `ssp` below are the two banks unconditionally, which is the fact a7/sp cannot express while the S bit is unknown to the reader.

usp.description: User stack pointer, registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5). Named because the active `sp`/`a7` is only one of the two banks and a debugger cannot tell which without decoding the S bit out of `sr`.

ssp.description: Supervisor stack pointer. Same registration, same reason.

emulator/run_to.$comment: protocol.md D12 — bounded, and it says whether it fired.

maxFrames.description: Bound. Without it an unreachable target is an unbounded run (D12).

reached.description: True = the condition fired. False = the run ended on maxFrames; NOTHING about the machine state follows from where it stopped.

caveat.description: SHOULD be present when reached is false.

emulator/checkpoint.$comment: protocol.md §6.1 / D13 — volatile, whole-machine, capped, refused loudly.

label.description: Optional human string; carried back verbatim, never interpreted.

id.description: The checkpoint handle. Server-assigned, never client-proposed (no cross-client collisions), and an OPAQUE STRING per D9 category 4 — not a slot index. A client hands it back to restore/checkpoint_drop and does nothing else with it. Pinned 2026-08-15 (protocol.md §6.1, §11.2); a numeric id here is non-conformant however plausible D9's earlier wording made it.

bytes.description: Snapshot size, so a client can see the cap coming.

emulator/restore.$comment: Restores the WHOLE machine, ROM included (D13 rule 2). Unknown id => -32005 unknownCheckpoint.

cursor.description: A continuation handle previously returned by this method. Opaque (D9 category 4): the client hands it back unexamined. Its BEHAVIOUR is normative — stable under concurrent mutation, never skipping or repeating a live item (protocol.md §6.1) — while its representation is deliberately the server's.

result.$comment: §2.4's FLAT spelling of the bounded-list rule, used because the list here IS the whole result rather than a field of one: the same field set as $defs/boundedList, as siblings of the array instead of wrapped around it. total/returned/limit registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5). Deliberately not unified onto the nested container — see §2.4's closing paragraph, which is also the one point this amendment says it would not argue with an owner who unified it.

total.description: Live checkpoints in total, not on this page.

returned.description: checkpoints.length, restated so a client can compare it to `total` without counting.

limit.description: The page ceiling actually applied, which is not necessarily the one the client asked for — a server clamps this to its checkpoint cap.

cursor.description: Present when more remain. Opaque (D9 category 4) — pass it back as the `cursor` param, unexamined.

truncated.description: Bounded/cursored like every list on this bus — a client must never mistake a partial list for a complete one.

emulator/pixel_attribution.$comment: protocol.md §6 (VRAM/CRAM/layers). Answers 'why is the dot at (x,y) the colour it is' against the VDP's CURRENT state — the server re-derives the scanline per call and reads no framebuffer, so on a free-running machine the answer is a live sample and the envelope's `running: true` is what says so (D11). A pure read: NOT subject to §6's run-control state rule.

x.description: Screen column, 0-based (D9 category 2 — a position a client counts with, not an address). Bounded here at the widest addressable value; the ACTIVE bound is the `width` this method reports, and a dot outside it is refused with -32004.

y.description: Screen line, 0-based. Same category and the same treatment as `x` — D9 names `line` among the JSON numbers, and this is that field.

width.description: Active display width the coordinates were resolved against (256 H32 / 320 H40). Reported so a client can bound its own sweep without first provoking a -32004.

height.description: Active display height (224, or 240 in V30).

layer.description: The displayed layer. camelCase values, matching the `runTo`/`runToScanline` stopped-reason spelling (protocol.md §3).

spriteIndex.description: SAT slot of the winning sprite. Present if and only if `layer` is 'sprite'. A slot index — D9 category 2.

cramIndex.description: The DISPLAYED colour's CRAM entry (palette*16 + nibble; the backdrop register's value for a backdrop dot). An index — D9 category 2.

cramAddr.$comment: The CRAM byte address of that entry (index*2). An address — D9 category 1, and `cramAddr` is the spelling emulator/write_cram already uses.

rgb.description: The colour actually put on the glass: the 3-bit channels run through the intensity ramp at the resolved shadow/highlight `state`. NOT the stored CRAM components — emulator/write_cram's r/g/b (0-7) are the stored colour, this is the displayed one, and the two differ whenever `state` is not 'normal'. Components, so JSON numbers (D9 category 2); 0-255 because that is the range the ramp emits.

state.description: The resolved shadow/highlight state applied to this dot's intensity (never its identity).

tile.description: Pattern index. A JSON number (D9 category 2) and NOT a hex string: arithmetic on it is meaningful and load-bearing — tile*32 is the VRAM address, and a multi-cell sprite's dot is base+offset. D9's category-4 test is 'a type a client must never compute on'; this is the opposite of that.

tileAddr.$comment: VRAM byte address of that pattern (tile*32, wrapped into VRAM). The address form, so a client can feed it straight to emulator/read_vram. A pattern is 32 bytes and cannot straddle the 64 KB wrap, so this plus 32 is the whole range.

cell.description: The winning nametable entry, decoded. Present if and only if `winner.layer` is planeA, planeB or window — a sprite or backdrop dot has no nametable cell.

x.description: Screen X of the sprite's top-left, (Xfield & 0x1FF) - 128. Signed: a sprite scrolling in from the left is legitimately negative.

baseTile.description: The sprite's base pattern index from its attribute word.

tile.description: The pattern this DOT is drawn from — base + (col*heightCells) + row after flips, column-major, wrapping. ABSENT when the winning sprite's box no longer contains the dot, which means the SAT was rewritten between the render and this query; the server reports the absence rather than inventing a tile.

tileAddr.$comment: VRAM byte address of `tile`. Present exactly when `tile` is.

satAddr.$comment: VRAM byte address of this sprite's 8-byte attribute-table entry (sat_base + index*8). This is the range a game writes when it moves, re-points or re-links the sprite — the answer to 'who MOVED this?' as opposed to 'who DREW this?'.

cacheDivergence.description: The cached Y/size/link disagree with VRAM at the current reg-5 base — the stale-SAT-cache state made visible (the Castlevania Bloodlines mixing). Present only when true.

sprite.description: The winning sprite, decoded. Present if and only if `winner.layer` is 'sprite'.

candidates.description: Every layer that could have shown at this dot, in VDP priority order, with why each won or lost. Deliberately NOT cursored: the list is bounded at 4 BY CONSTRUCTION (at most one flattened sprite pixel, the plane-A slot, plane B, and the backdrop), not by a server policy a client would have to page around. A live dot yields 3 or 4 entries; a BLANKED dot (display off, or the leftmost-column blank at x<8) yields exactly one — the backdrop, verdict 'won' — which is why minItems is 1 and not 3.

cramIndex.description: The colour this layer WOULD have shown.

verdict.description: won = displayed. lostToPriority = opaque, but outranked. transparent = colour nibble 0, contributes nothing. operator = an opaque sprite operator (palette 3, nibble 14/15) that outranks the winner but is not drawn — it shifted the winner's shadow/highlight state instead.
